body.justification: Matching lower and feasible-estimator upper bounds hold over the same enlarged class with all donors used once.
body.gap: The proof allows heterogeneous bounded responses and design-only geometric beta mixing, and it uses no covariance estimator.
body.consumer: Designers can locate the active replication, spacing, or donor-precision channel.
body.proof_tex:
For a channel \(q\), take \((P_{0,q},P_{1,q})\) from \texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding}, write their conditional target values as \(\theta_0,\theta_1\), and put \(\Delta_q=|\theta_1-\theta_0|\).  Their conditional testing affinity is at least a fixed \(a_0>0\), and \(\Delta_q^2\ge cR_q\).  For any observed-data estimator \(\widetilde\tau\), the events
\[
E'_0=\{|\widetilde\tau-\theta_0|\ge\Delta_q/2\},
\qquad
E'_1=\{|\widetilde\tau-\theta_1|\ge\Delta_q/2\}
\]
cover the sample space.  Integration against the overlap measure therefore gives
\[
P_{0,q}(E'_0\mid E_0)+P_{1,q}(E'_1\mid E_0)\ge a_0,
\]
and hence
\[
\max_{\ell\in\{0,1\}}
\mathbb E_{P_{\ell,q}}
[(\widetilde\tau-\theta_\ell)^2\mid E_0]
\ge\frac{a_0\Delta_q^2}{8}\ge cR_q.
\tag{42}
\]
Maximizing over the four channels, using \(R_{\star,\beta}=\max_qR_q\), and then taking the supremum over \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\) and infimum over estimators proves the minimax lower bound.

For the upper bound let
\[
\mathscr X=\sigma\{X_{st}:s\le S,\ t\le T\},
\]
and condition on \((\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)_{j=1}^{N})\).  On the event of successful fits, \texttt{lem:identification-fwl} and the linear representation in \texttt{def:honest-interval} give
\[
\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0)
=U_{\mathrm{evt}}-U_{\mathrm{hist}}-B_{\mathrm{LP}}-B_{\mathrm{don}},
\tag{43}
\]
where
\[
U_{\mathrm{evt}}=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}
\{B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0]\},
\]
\[
U_{\mathrm{hist}}=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\pi_s
\sum_{t=1}^{T}a_{sti}\varepsilon_{sti},
\]
\[
B_{\mathrm{LP}}=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
\left\{\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}a_{sti}m_s(X_{st})
-m_s(\widetilde z_s)\right\},
\]
\[
B_{\mathrm{don}}=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
\{m_s(\widetilde z_s)-m_s(z_{0s})\}.
\]
The two full-design restrictions center the first two sums under the displayed conditioning; donor independence permits the donor sample to be adjoined.  Conditional cross-unit independence and the response range bound imply
\[
\mathbb E_P[U_{\mathrm{evt}}^2\mid\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)]
\le B^2\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}=B^2R_{\mathrm{tr}}.
\tag{44}
\]
Treating the entire response history of one unit as one cluster, \texttt{lem:full-data-local-polynomial-control} similarly gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_P[U_{\mathrm{hist}}^2\mid\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)]
&\le B^2\sum_{s=1}^{S}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}
\left[\pi_s\sum_t|a_{sti}|\right]^2\\
&\le B^2c_G^{-1}R_{\mathrm{tr}}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{45}
\]
No temporal outcome restriction and no identical response law is used in (45).

Let \(C_K\) bound the Euclidean radius of the support of \(K\).  Whenever \(w_{st}>0\),
\(\|X_{st}-\widetilde z_s\|_2\le C_Kh_s\).  Polynomial reproduction, the H\"older Taylor remainder, and the deterministic absolute-weight bound give
\[
|B_{\mathrm{LP}}|\le C\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_sh_s^\lambda.
\tag{46}
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\((\sum_s\pi_sh_s^\lambda)^2\le S\sum_s\pi_s^2h_s^{2\lambda}\).  Apply \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-selector-control} with exponent \(2\lambda\), conditionally on \(\widetilde z_s\), and then integrate over the donor sample.  Because \(S\) and the positive weights are fixed,
\[
\mathbb E_P[B_{\mathrm{LP}}^2\mathbf1_{\mathrm{good}}\mid E_0]
\le C\{R_{\mathrm{sm}}+R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}+N^{-\lambda}\}
\le CR_{\star,\beta},
\tag{47}
\]
where \(N^{-\lambda}\le N^{-\kappa}\) follows from \(\kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\}\).

Put \(D=Sd\) and define the proof variables
\[
Y_j=\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0),
\qquad
W_N=N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{N}Y_j.
\]
Donor replication gives conditionally independent mean-zero vectors with
\(\mathbb E_P[Y_jY_j^\top\mid E_0]=I_D\).  On expanding \(\|W_N\|_2^4\), every term containing a singleton sample index has conditional expectation zero.  The all-equal terms and the three pairings give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_P[\|W_N\|_2^4\mid E_0]
&=\frac1N\mathbb E_P[\|Y_1\|_2^4\mid E_0]\\
&\quad+\left(1-\frac1N\right)
\{(\operatorname{tr}I_D)^2+2\operatorname{tr}(I_D^2)\}\\
&\le\frac BN+\left(1-\frac1N\right)(D^2+2D)=M_4(N).
\end{aligned}
\tag{48}
\]
Consequently
\[
\mathbb E_P[\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(\bar Z-z_0)\|_2^4\mid E_0]
\le CN^{-2}.
\tag{49}
\]
Euclidean projection onto the cube cannot increase distance from \(z_0\), and the covariance eigenvalue bounds imply
\[
\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(\widetilde z-z_0)\|_2
\le\sqrt{C_\Sigma/c_\Sigma}\,
\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(\bar Z-z_0)\|_2.
\tag{50}
\]
On the event where the left side of (50) is at most \(\delta_0\), the upper local-modulus inequality bounds \(|B_{\mathrm{don}}|^2\) by a fixed constant times that norm to the power \(2\kappa\).  Lyapunov's inequality and (49) bound its expectation by \(CN^{-\kappa}\).  On the complementary event, boundedness gives \(|B_{\mathrm{don}}|\le B\), while Markov's inequality and (49) make the event probability \(O(N^{-2})\).  Since \(0<\kappa\le1\),
\[
\mathbb E_P[B_{\mathrm{don}}^2\mid E_0]
\le CN^{-\kappa}=CR_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{51}
\]

Every successful intercept satisfies
\[
|\widehat m_s|\le B\sum_{t,i}|a_{sti}|\le Bc_G^{-1/2},
\]
and a failed intercept contribution is zero.  Thus the squared estimation error is uniformly bounded on the bad sample.  The bad-sample probability bound in \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-selector-control} makes that contribution at most \(CR_{\star,\beta}\) along the asserted arrays.  Combining (43)--(51) with
\((x_1+x_2+x_3+x_4)^2\le4\sum_{j=1}^{4}x_j^2\) proves
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)}
\mathbb E_P[(\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0]
\le CR_{\star,\beta}.
\tag{52}
\]
The same quantity upper-bounds the minimax infimum because \(\widehat\tau\) is one observed-data estimator, independent of the unknown \(\Sigma\).

For completeness, set \(a=2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)\).  For every integer \(T\ge3\), weighted arithmetic--geometric mean and \(\log T\ge1\) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
&=(n_s^{-1})^a(T^{-2\lambda/d})^{1-a}\\
&\le an_s^{-1}+(1-a)R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}.
\end{aligned}
\]
After multiplying by \(\pi_s^2\), summing, and using \(\sum_s\pi_s^2\le1\),
\[
R_{\mathrm{sm}}
\le aR_{\mathrm{tr}}+(1-a)R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}
\le R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}.
\tag{53}
\]
Thus
\[
R_{\star,\beta}=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}
\qquad(T\ge3).
\]
Equations (42) and (52) establish the same-class bracket in every relative-growth regime.  The full donor covariance enters through the standardized modulus and (50), but neither the estimator nor the proof estimates it.
